"'''Joan Is Awful'''" is the first episode of the sixth series of the anthology series ''[[Black Mirror]]''. It was written by the series creator [[Charlie Brooker]] and directed by [[Ally Pankiw]]. Alongside the rest of the sixth series, it premiered on [[Netflix]] on 15 June 2023. It follows Joan ([[Annie Murphy]]) as her life is adapted in real-time into a television series starring [[Salma Hayek]]. It is released on a fictional [[streaming television|streaming service]], Streamberry, that parodies Netflix; Brooker said the company had no objections to its portrayal. Marketing for the sixth series featured Streamberry and personalised ''Is Awful'' [[thumbnail]]s.

Brooker described "Joan Is Awful" as the only episode of the series to fit the show's traditional style. It was inspired by the recency of the events depicted in ''[[The Dropout]]'' (2022); Joan was written with Murphy in mind after Brooker watched ''[[Schitt's Creek]]'' (2015–2020). Hayek encouraged more profane dialogue than was in the script for her character, and the addition of facts about herself.

Pankiw saw the episode as exploring questions about who can make art and tell stories; the women-led stories and a diversity of crew were important to her. Reviewers identified themes including [[streaming service]]s, [[Synthetic media|personalised content]] and privacy. It was considered timely as its writing preceded the release of [[ChatGPT]] and [[2023 Hollywood labor disputes|2023 Hollywood strikes]] by the [[2023 Writers Guild of America strike|Writers Guild of America]] and actors' union [[2023 SAG-AFTRA strike|SAG-AFTRA]], which drew attention to the role of [[artificial intelligence]] and [[computer-generated imagery]] of actors in entertainment industries.

The episode is more comedic than most ''Black Mirror'' episodes and has a happy ending. Reviewers praised its tone and the acting of Murphy and Hayek. However, the episode's pacing and plot received an ambivalent response. Some critics disliked the execution of its themes. The episode makes numerous [[Easter egg (media)|Easter egg]] references to other ''Black Mirror'' installments through Streamberry's platform and use of the song "[[Anyone Who Knows What Love Is (Will Understand)]]".

==Plot==
Joan Tait ([[Annie Murphy]]) wakes up, eats breakfast made by her fiancé Krish ([[Avi Nash]]) and drives to work while [[lip syncing]] to [[Saweetie]]'s rap "[[Tap In]]". Under instruction from the [[board of directors]], she fires Sandy ([[Ayo Edebiri]]), who worked to reduce the company's [[carbon emissions]]. In therapy, Joan contrasts Krish's blandness with her ex-boyfriend Mac ([[Rob Delaney]]) who is messaging her. She meets Mac for dinner and they kiss.

Joan and Krish discover a Streamberry show titled ''Joan Is Awful''. Depicted by [[Salma Hayek]], the unlikeable, fictionalised version of Joan plays out events from Joan's day. Krish leaves after seeing the fictional Mac ([[Ben Barnes (actor)|Ben Barnes]]) and Joan kiss. The programme shows Hayek's Joan discovering ''Joan Is Awful'', with its own version of Joan ([[Cate Blanchett]]), before Hayek's Joan is left by Krish ([[Himesh Patel]]).

Joan is fired due to the show and told by a lawyer ([[Lolly Adefope]]) that Streamberry's actions are legal due to their [[terms and conditions]]. The show is made by a cutting-edge [[quantum computer]] using [[Computer-generated imagery|CGI]]-based [[virtual actor]]s and [[real-time data]] gathered from Joan's devices.

To get a reaction from Hayek, Joan—with a penis drawn on her forehead—dresses as a cheerleader and defecates in a church, interrupting a wedding. After this is depicted in ''Joan Is Awful'', Hayek speaks to a lawyer who says that Streamberry can use her [[Personality rights|likeness]] and [[Personal information|personalities]] like this as she has licensed it to them. Hayek meets with Joan and they plot to destroy the quantum computer.

Hayek persuades a receptionist to allow her into Streamberry's office and lets Joan in. They pass the [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] Mona Javadi ([[Leila Farzad]]), who explains to the journalist Fatima Klaas (Danielle Vitalis) that Streamberry plans personalised, computer-generated content for all users. Joan was chosen as she is completely average, while the negativity of the ''Is Awful'' brand maximises [[engagement marketing|engagement]].

Joan and Hayek reach a [[technician]], Beppe ([[Michael Cera]]), who reveals that they are in a [[simulated reality]] where Joan is based on a Source Joan ([[Kayla Lorette]]) with a likeness of Annie Murphy. Javadi arrives and begs Joan not to destroy the quantum computer, which would destroy all realities above theirs. Joan realises that Source Joan has already decided to smash the computer and follows suit.

In the source reality, Source Joan and Annie Murphy celebrate as friends, though they are on [[house arrest]]. Source Joan starts a coffee shop, a dream of hers that she shared with her therapist.

A [[post-credits scene]] shows Source Joan's church defecation.

Streamberry parodies Netflix, imitating its graphic design, user interface and 'tudum' [[sound logo]].<ref name="Indy Streamberry"/> Brooker said that Netflix were immediately supportive of this idea.<ref name="Tele interview"/> In one draft, Joan's Streamberry account displayed each of the series six episodes.<ref name="Esquire interview"/> Marketing for the episode included a mockup of Streamberry's website, streamberry.tv, as well as Netflix social media accounts briefly changing their names to Streamberry. The tie-in website youareawful.com allows users to create personalised ''Is Awful'' [[thumbnail]]s.<ref name="Indy Streamberry">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/black-mirror-netflix-streamberry-joan-is-awful-b2360709.html|title=Netflix releases fake Streamberry website based on Black Mirror episode 'Joan Is Awful'|work=[[The Independent]]|last=Lewis|first=Isobel|date=20 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=29 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230629183944/http://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/black-mirror-netflix-streamberry-joan-is-awful-b2360709.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Billboards with fans' ''Is Awful'' images were used to promote the sixth series in the UK.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theregister.com/2023/06/26/joan_black_mirror_terms/|title='Joan Is Awful' Black Mirror episode rebounds on Netflix|work=[[The Register]]|last=Hardcastle|first=Jessica Lyons|date=26 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=22 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230822192113/https://www.theregister.com/2023/06/26/joan_black_mirror_terms/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/tvfilm/black-mirror-joan-is-awful-fan-posters-b1089623.html|title=You Are Awful: Black Mirror creates 'Joan is Awful' posters of fans|work=[[Evening Standard]]|last=Loffhagen|first=Emma|date=22 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=22 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230822192116/https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/tvfilm/black-mirror-joan-is-awful-fan-posters-b1089623.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Writing===
Brooker was the screenwriter for "Joan Is Awful".<ref name="Titles, cast, crew">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-episode-titles-photos/|title=''Black Mirror'' season 6 reveals episode details, new photos|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last=Holub|first=Christian|date=11 May 2023|accessdate=24 July 2023|archive-date=15 June 2023|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20230615060641/https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-episode-titles-photos/|url-status=live}}</ref> He said it was the only episode of the sixth series to feel like a traditional installment,<ref name="Esquire interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44197628/charlie-brooker-black-mirror-interview/|title=''Black Mirror'' Season 6: Charlie Brooker Breaks Down Every Episode|work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|last=Stefansky|first=Emma|date=15 June 2023|access-date=17 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616145405/https://www.esquire.com/entertainment/tv/a44197628/charlie-brooker-black-mirror-interview/|url-status=live}}</ref> albeit more "overtly comic".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-season-6-red-mirror-newsupdate/|title=''Black Mirror'' creator Charlie Brooker explains 'Red Mirror' label|work=[[Radio Times]]|last1=Griffin|first1=Louise|last2=Cormack|first2=Morgan|date=15 June 2023|access-date=17 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616225949/https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-season-6-red-mirror-newsupdate/|url-status=live}}</ref> An early idea had Joan the subject of newspaper headlines over petty colleague complaints. Another saw news networks using [[deepfake]]s of politicians to create [[fake news]]. Brooker was later inspired by the miniseries ''[[The Dropout]]'' (2022), which depicted the creation and downfall of a disgraced tech startup, [[Theranos]]. Brooker said it seemed to make drama from "things that happened ten minutes ago",<ref name="Esquire interview"/><ref name="NME interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/features/tv-features/black-mirror-netflix-interview-charlie-brooker-cast-episodes-theories-3457066|title=''Black Mirror'' season six post-watch guide: trivia, set secrets and more|work=[[NME]]|last=Flood|first=Alex|date=16 June 2023|access-date=16 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616174102/https://www.nme.com/features/tv-features/black-mirror-netflix-interview-charlie-brooker-cast-episodes-theories-3457066|url-status=live}}</ref> and depicted events that the writers could not have had insight into, such as a person dancing with her partner.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/63637b80-d811-49e7-8eea-3bc268fcb480|title=Charlie Brooker on satirising TV in Black Mirror: 'If it wasn't on Netflix, we'd be sued'|work=[[Financial Times]]|last=Harrod|first=Horatia|date=7 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=24 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230824003858/https://www.ft.com/content/63637b80-d811-49e7-8eea-3bc268fcb480|url-status=live}}</ref> He also reflected on incidents of ordinary people becoming a "whipping boy" on social media.<ref name="Vanity Fair">{{cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-six-charlie-brooker-spoilers|title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s Charlie Brooker Keeps Finding New Ways to Freak Us Out|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|last=Press|first=Joy|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616162024/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-six-charlie-brooker-spoilers|url-status=live}}</ref>

Filming finished before the chatbot [[ChatGPT]] was released; Brooker was happy with the episode's timeliness. Brooker commented that the entertainment industry was considering a future of "automatically generated entertainment that is endlessly targeted directly at individuals" and what this would mean for writers.<ref name="Esquire interview"/> He said ChatGPT could be useful to writers, like [[Adobe Photoshop]] to artists, but executives' use of it posed worries.<ref name="Vanity Fair"/> In Brooker's view, ChatGPT does not have the capacity to think but is "an impersonator".<ref name="Tele interview">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/16/charlie-brooker-interview-ai-black-mirror-series-six/|title=Black Mirror creator Charlie Brooker: 'I've worked out how to beat AI'|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Rees|first=Jasper|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=24 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230824003916/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/16/charlie-brooker-interview-ai-black-mirror-series-six/|url-status=live}}</ref>

An April 2023 casting announcement for ''Black Mirror'' named Annie Murphy, Salma Hayek Pinault, Michael Cera, Himesh Patel, Rob Delaney, and Ben Barnes.<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Strause |first1=Jackie |title=''Black Mirror'' Sets Season 6 Return, Reveals Cast and Teaser Trailer |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/black-mirror-season-6-return-cast-trailer-1235402653/ |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230515011918/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/black-mirror-season-6-return-cast-trailer-1235402653/ |archive-date=15 May 2023 |date=26 April 2023 |url-status=live |access-date=15 June 2023}}</ref> The director was [[Ally Pankiw]]; she saw diversity of the crew in gender and sexuality as important.<ref name="THR"/> Udo Kramer designed sets for all series six episodes.<ref name="Dezeen">{{cite web|url=https://www.dezeen.com/2023/06/15/black-mirror-production-designer-interview/|title=Black Mirror's latest season a 'mini film festival' says production designer Udo Kramer|work=[[Dezeen]]|last=Carlson|first=Cajsa|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=7 August 2023|archive-date=21 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721213711/https://www.dezeen.com/2023/06/15/black-mirror-production-designer-interview/|url-status=live}}</ref> The soundtrack was composed by Ames Bessada, with whom Pankiw had previously worked, and released on 21 July 2023.<ref name="THR"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://filmmusicreporter.com/2023/07/20/soundtrack-album-for-black-mirror-episode-joan-is-awful-to-be-released/|title=Soundtrack Album for 'Black Mirror' Episode 'Joan Is Awful' Released|work=Film Music Reporter|date=20 July 2023|accessdate=10 August 2023|archive-date=24 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230824003856/https://filmmusicreporter.com/2023/07/20/soundtrack-album-for-black-mirror-episode-joan-is-awful-to-be-released/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Filming took place in September 2022,<ref name="Today"/> with "Red Book" used as a codename.<ref name="BBC Sounds"/> An American-style bungalow in [[Crowthorne]], England, was used for exterior filming. The owner Jennifer Johnston purchased it with film production usage in mind. According to Johnston, the production crew—numbering 70—added rock gardens and repainted it, also adding shrubs and American postboxes to neighbouring houses.<ref name="BBC Sounds">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/p0fv9knh|title=Salma Hayek lives in my house in Black Mirror|last=Buckley|first=Bill|work=[[BBC Radio Berkshire]]|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=15 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715093849/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/p0fv9knh|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bracknellnews.co.uk/news/23586157.black-mirror-episode-filmed-crowthorne-starring-salma-hayek/|title=Black Mirror episode filmed in Crowthorne, starring Salma Hayek|work=[[Bracknell News]]|date=13 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=15 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715093849/https://www.bracknellnews.co.uk/news/23586157.black-mirror-episode-filmed-crowthorne-starring-salma-hayek/|url-status=live}}</ref> The Streamberry office used white, black and red colours to evoke the Netflix logo.<ref name="Dezeen"/>

Murphy and Pankiw worked on the comedy series ''[[Schitt's Creek]]'' (2015–2020), which is referenced in the episode's dialogue.<ref name="CBC">{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/annie-murphy-black-mirror-1.6878260|title=Annie Murphy on Black Mirror's AI acting fears — and that Schitt's Creek call-out|publisher=[[CBC.ca]]|last=Weaver|first=Jackson|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=17 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230717192904/https://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/annie-murphy-black-mirror-1.6878260|url-status=live}}</ref> Brooker wrote Joan with Murphy in mind, having recently watched the series. He saw her as "likeable yet relatable, goofy, and flawed".<ref name="BuzzFeed">{{cite web|url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/sam_cleal/black-mirror-netflix-facts|date=16 June 2023|title=Here Are 17 Interesting "Black Mirror" Season Six Facts We Learned In Conversation With Charlie Brooker|last=Cleal|first=Sam|website=[[BuzzFeed News]]|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=18 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230618202937/https://www.buzzfeed.com/sam_cleal/black-mirror-netflix-facts|url-status=live}}</ref> Murphy was keen to participate before reading the episode's script.<ref name="Today">{{cite web|url=https://www.today.com/popculture/tv/black-mirror-joan-is-awful-annie-murphy-interview-rcna89542|title=Annie Murphy's 'Black Mirror' episode, 'Joan Is Awful,' is about the future of AI. It 'terrifies' her|work=[[Today (American TV program)|Today]]|last=Miller|first=Ayanna|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=22 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230822192119/https://www.today.com/popculture/tv/black-mirror-joan-is-awful-annie-murphy-interview-rcna89542|url-status=live}}</ref> She described being confused at playing herself towards the end of the episode, in contrast to Cera, who seemed to thoroughly understand the story.<ref name="EW interview"/>

Hayek said that playing a fictionalised version of herself allowed for self-deprecation and exploration of people's impressions of her.<ref name="NME Hayek">{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/news/tv/salma-hayek-was-worried-black-mirror-role-would-get-her-in-trouble-3457095|title=Salma Hayek was worried ''Black Mirror'' role would get her 'in trouble'|work=[[NME]]|last=Edwards|first=Chris|date=16 June 2023|access-date=16 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616184939/https://www.nme.com/news/tv/salma-hayek-was-worried-black-mirror-role-would-get-her-in-trouble-3457095|url-status=live}}</ref> She had experienced her likeness being used online in "disrespectful ways".<ref name="EW interview">{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-premiere-break-down/|title=Let's break down that mind-blowing Black Mirror season 6 premiere|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|last=Holub|first=Christian|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=19 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819102128/https://ew.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-premiere-break-down/|url-status=live}}</ref> Brooker said that they wrote "more tame" lines so as not to "scare her off", but Hayek encouraged "outrageous" dialogue.<ref name="NME interview"/> Hayek suggested use of facts about her in the script, leading to mention of her [[dyslexia]] and [[Roman Catholicism]].<ref name="BuzzFeed" /> Murphy said of the scene where her character defecates in a church: "I couldn't be more excited about it and I could picture it".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/ustv/a44221169/black-mirror-annie-murphy-gross-scene/|title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s 'Joan Is Awful' star on filming 'gross' scene|work=[[Digital Spy]]|last=Rowan|first=Iona|date=16 June 2023|access-date=16 June 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616235511/https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/ustv/a44221169/black-mirror-annie-murphy-gross-scene/|url-status=live}}</ref> Hayek, however, did question whether she would get in trouble for her role in the episode.<ref name="NME Hayek"/> During filming, crew adopted [[pigtail]]s in "solidarity" with Joan, according to Pankiw.<ref name="THR">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/black-mirror-annie-murphy-joan-is-awful-director-interview-1235518988/|title=Annie Murphy and 'Black Mirror' Director on 'Joan Is Awful's' Feminist Themes and 'Spookily Timely' AI Story|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|last=White|first=Abbey|date=19 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=18 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230718211420/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/black-mirror-annie-murphy-joan-is-awful-director-interview-1235518988/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Pankiw believed the episode asked "who gets to make art?" and "what happens when we consume other people's stories?" She saw the perception of women in media by other women as a [[feminist]] theme and liked that the episode had prominent female friendships and women seeking autonomy. Murphy found that Joan's cooperation with Hayek made for an "uplifting female empowerment" story.<ref name="THR"/>

==Analysis==
The episode is a comedy: ''[[i (newspaper)|i]]''{{'}}s Emily Bootle called it one of the "most explicitly funny" installments of the programme.<ref name="i">{{cite web|url=https://inews.co.uk/culture/television/black-mirror-joan-awful-netflix-review-shock-2412161|title=Black Mirror: Joan is Awful, Netflix, review: Without the power to shock, Brooker is making us laugh|work=[[i (newspaper)|i]]|last=Bootle|first=Emily|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=24 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230824003854/https://inews.co.uk/culture/television/black-mirror-joan-awful-netflix-review-shock-2412161|url-status=live}}</ref> It was considered a [[cringe comedy]] and a [[dark comedy]] by ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]''{{'}}s Judy Berman and ''[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]''{{'}}s Emma Stefansky, respectively, and Alex Cranz of ''[[The Verge]]'' commented that it was "gentler" than other episodes.<ref name="Time">{{cite magazine|url=https://time.com/6287513/black-mirror-season-6-review/|title=What Even Is ''Black Mirror'' Anymore?|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|last=Berman|first=Judy|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=15 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715005440/https://time.com/6287513/black-mirror-season-6-review/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Esquire interview"/><ref name="Verge">{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/23763339/black-mirrors-joan-is-awful-netflix-future-streaming|title=Black Mirror's 'Joan is Awful' shits all over the future of streaming|work=[[The Verge]]|last=Cranz|first=Alex|date=17 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=10 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810095610/https://www.theverge.com/23763339/black-mirrors-joan-is-awful-netflix-future-streaming|url-status=live}}</ref> It was compared to the first episode, "[[The National Anthem (Black Mirror)|The National Anthem]]", wherein a prime minister is made to have sex with a pig. "The National Anthem" also had a near-future setting and, according to ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]''{{'}}s Ed Power, "juvenile humour".<ref name="DoG review"/><ref name="Tele">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/15/black-mirror-season-6-e1-review-joan-awful-ai/|title='Joan is Awful' is ''Black Mirror'' at its most self-satisfied – and makes for a tiresome opener|work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Power|first=Ed|date=15 June 2023|access-date=23 August 2023|archive-date=9 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230809225018/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/tv/2023/06/15/black-mirror-season-6-e1-review-joan-awful-ai/|url-status=live}}</ref> In ''[[The Independent]]'', Nick Hilton said both works were "[[Orwellian]] farce".<ref name="Indy">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-episodes-ranked-b2357292.html|title=''Black Mirror'' season six review: Charlie Brooker's sci-fi mishmash needs to stop messing with a winning formula|work=[[The Independent]]|last=Hilton|first=Nick|date=15 June 2023|access-date=23 August 2023|archive-date=16 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616020939/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-episodes-ranked-b2357292.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Black Mirror'' was released by Netflix from 2016 onwards; it made an [[interactive film]] specific to this new medium with ''[[Black Mirror: Bandersnatch|Bandersnatch]]'' (2018). [[Streaming service]]s such as Netflix are the subject of "Joan Is Awful", as well as the following episode, "[[Loch Henry]]" and season 7 episode, "[[Hotel Reverie]]".<ref name="Variety">{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-1235644259/|title='Black Mirror' Season 6 Is a Refreshingly Uncynical Return to Form: TV Review|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|last=D'Addario|first=Daniel|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=25 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625033800/https://variety.com/2023/tv/reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-1235644259/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Time"/> Richard Lawson, a ''[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]'' critic, saw it as commenting on Netflix's algorithm-led strategy, while Power believed it was about [[binge-watching]].<ref name="Vanity review">{{cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=''Black Mirror''{{'}}s Odd Future Feels Stuck in the Past|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|last=Lawson|first=Richard|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=20 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620063648/https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/06/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Tele"/> Power said Javadi parodies [[Bela Bajaria]], Netflix's Chief Content Officer, while Joan's life resembles the protagonist of ''[[The Truman Show]]'' (1998).<ref name="Tele"/>

Other themes include [[artificial intelligence]] (AI) and personalised content. ''Black Mirror'' previously explored AI in "[[Be Right Back]]", which features a robotic replacement for a grieving woman's dead partner.<ref name="Tele interview"/> Amit Katwala analysed that personalised content posed threats to publications such as ''[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]'', which he was writing in, as they rely on common cultural experiences. Katwala suggested that [[large language model]]s might then generate personalised articles about the personalised content.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/story/black-mirror-joan-is-awful-click-here/|title=Please Click This Link About Black Mirror's 'Joan Is Awful' Episode|magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]]|last=Katwala|first=Amit|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=23 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230723125400/https://www.wired.com/story/black-mirror-joan-is-awful-click-here/|url-status=live}}</ref> Privacy was also a motif: Lawson found the episode to satirise nosy neighbours, while Bootle saw it as about [[Big Brother (Nineteen Eighty-Four)|Big Brother]]-style invasion of privacy through data collection.<ref name="Vanity review"/><ref name="i"/>

The episode makes liberal use of [[Easter egg (media)|Easter egg]] references to other installments. The song "[[Anyone Who Knows What Love Is (Will Understand)]]" by [[Irma Thomas]] is heard when Joan meets Mac at a restaurant, marking its sixth use in the programme.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-soundtrack-songs-call-back-to-the-series-past/|title=Black Mirror Season 6 Soundtrack: Songs Call Back to the Series' Past|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Arens|first=Brynna|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628024938/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-soundtrack-songs-call-back-to-the-series-past/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.radiotimes.com/tv/sci-fi/black-mirror-soundtrack-every-song-in-season-6-of-the-netflix-anthology/|title=Black Mirror soundtrack: Every song in season 6 of the Netflix anthology|work=[[Radio Times]]|last=Hibbs|first=James|date=20 June 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023}}</ref> The Streamberry platform shows programmes such as ''Junipero Dreaming''—named after "[[San Junipero]]"—and ''Finding Ritman''—about ''Bandersnatch''{{'}}s Colin Ritman. It contains thumbnails for fictional shows seen in other episodes (''Sea of Tranquility'' and ''Hot Shots''), and the cartoon ''Rowdy and Peanut'', named after characters in Brooker's ''[[Cat Burglar]]'' (2022).<ref name="DoG egg">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-easter-eggs-upend-the-shows-shared-universe/|title=Black Mirror Season 6 Easter Eggs Upend the Show's Shared Universe|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last1=Bojalad|first1=Alec|last2=Mellor|first2=Louisa|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=20 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720212347/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-season-6-easter-eggs-upend-the-shows-shared-universe/|url-status=live}}</ref> Streamberry is also key to the following episode, "Loch Henry", wherein a character produces a documentary—''Loch Henry: Truth Will Out''—that can be seen on Joan's account.<ref name="DoG egg"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/why-you-should-watch-black-mirror-season-6-in-reverse-order/|title=Why You Should Watch Black Mirror Season 6 in Reverse Order|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Harrisson|first=Juliette|date=21 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=3 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703084812/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/why-you-should-watch-black-mirror-season-6-in-reverse-order/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:AI Protest Sign 2023 WGA Strike.jpg|thumb|alt=WGA picket sign against AI replacement|upright|A WGA picketer holds a sign protesting replacement of writers with [[artificial intelligence]].]]
"Joan Is Awful" was seen as prescient for its portrayal of a television series made with no human input.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/cultural-comment/hollywood-self-sabotage-writer-strike|title=Hollywood's Slo-Mo Self-Sabotage|magazine=[[The New Yorker]]|last=Kang|first=Inkoo|date=30 July 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=22 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230822192113/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/cultural-comment/hollywood-self-sabotage-writer-strike|url-status=live}}</ref> It was written shortly before the 2023 strikes by the [[2023 Writers Guild of America strike|Writers Guild of America]] (WGA) and actors' union [[2023 SAG-AFTRA strike|SAG-AFTRA]], who negotiated the role of AI in entertainment with the [[Alliance of Motion Picture and Television Producers]] (AMPTP).<ref name="THR"/> An anonymous SAG-AFTRA member told ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' that actors saw it as "a documentary of the future, with their likenesses sold off and used any way producers and studios want";<ref>{{cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=11 July 2023 |title=SAG-AFTRA Strike Could Hinge On AI; Deep Divisions Remain Between Actors & Studios In Final Hours Of Talks |url=https://deadline.com/2023/07/actors-strike-ai-kim-kardashian-fran-drescher-contract-deadline-1235432142/ |access-date=22 August 2023 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-date=10 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230810100248/https://deadline.com/2023/07/actors-strike-ai-kim-kardashian-fran-drescher-contract-deadline-1235432142/ |url-status=live }}</ref> WGA members feared job losses from computer-generated scripts.<ref>{{cite web |last=Heritage |first=Stuart |date=13 July 2023 |title='Joan Is Awful': ''Black Mirror'' episode is every striking actor's worst nightmare |work=[[The Guardian]] |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2023/jul/13/joan-is-awful-black-mirror-striking-actors-nightmare |access-date=22 August 2023 |archive-date=13 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230713140421/https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2023/jul/13/joan-is-awful-black-mirror-striking-actors-nightmare |url-status=live }}</ref> The AMPTP proposed that actors be paid for a day of digital scanning so that their likeness could be used as background characters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2023/7/13/23794224/sag-aftra-actors-strike-ai-image-rights|title=Actors say Hollywood studios want their AI replicas — for free, forever|work=[[The Verge]]|last=Webster|first=Andrew|date=13 July 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=15 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230715134352/https://www.theverge.com/2023/7/13/23794224/sag-aftra-actors-strike-ai-image-rights|url-status=live}}</ref> In contrast, SAG-AFTRA demanded "informed consent and fair compensation" for use of a person's likeness or performance to be altered with AI.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/ai-in-hollywood-strike-guild-demands.html|title=How Hollywood Is Avoiding Robot Overlords|work=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]|last=Frank|first=Jason P.|date=20 July 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023|archive-date=21 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721000735/https://www.vulture.com/article/ai-in-hollywood-strike-guild-demands.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The WGA aimed to prohibit AI's usage in scriptwriting.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2023/07/sag-aftra-strike-studios-ai-proposal-sounds-like-black-mirror-right|title=SAG-AFTRA Strike: Studios' AI Proposal Sounds Like Black Mirror, Right?|work=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|last=Jarvey|first=Natalie|date=13 July 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023}}</ref> Pankiw expressed support for the WGA strike when introducing the episode at a live screening.<ref name="THR"/>

==Reception==
Despite an approval rating of 94% based on 17 reviews from [[Rotten Tomatoes]],<ref>{{cite Rotten Tomatoes |type=tv |id=black_mirror |season=6 |episode=1 |access-date=22 June 2023}}</ref> critical response varied. While ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' and ''[[Salon.com|Salon]]'' described it as the best of the sixth series, ''The Daily Telegraph'' and ''[[The A.V. Club]]'' saw it as the worst.<ref name="RS"/><ref name="Salon"/><ref name="Tele"/><ref name="AVClub"/> It garnered ratings of four out of five stars in ''[[Den of Geek]]'' and ''i'',<ref name="DoG review"/><ref name="i"/> three stars in ''The Independent'' and ''[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]'',<ref name="Indy"/><ref name="Vulture"/> and two stars in ''The Daily Telegraph''.<ref name="Tele"/>

Reviewers widely acknowledged the episode as timely for its themes.<ref name="Paste"/><ref name="Vanity review"/><ref name="Salon"/> However, writing in ''[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]'', Leila Jordan did not find it sufficiently "surprising or introspective".<ref name="Paste"/> Lawson stated that "Loch Henry", a "predictable but compelling thriller", explored the same ideas better.<ref name="Paste">{{cite web|url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/netflix/black-mirror-season-6-review|title=''Black Mirror'' Struggles to Imagine the Future in an Uneven Season 6|work=[[Paste (magazine)|Paste]]|last=Jordan|first=Leila|date=16 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=24 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724170744/https://www.pastemagazine.com/tv/netflix/black-mirror-season-6-review|url-status=live}}</ref> Jordan praised the satire of Netflix.<ref name="Paste"/> Contrastingly, Cranz questioned the episode's logic, including the appeal of ''Is Awful'' series and the nature of the simulated realities.<ref name="Verge"/> In addition, ''[[Mashable]]''{{'}}s Chris Taylor criticised it as an example of satire enabling "pretty awful things" when the target "learns to play along", comparing it to [[Mattel]]'s villainous role in ''[[Barbie (film)|Barbie]]'' (2023) or the prominence that the politician [[Boris Johnson]] gained from appearing on ''[[Have I Got News for You]]'' (1990–).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mashable.com/article/streamberry-netflix-black-mirror-satire|title=Sorry Netflix, Streamberry isn't funny|work=[[Mashable]]|last=Taylor|first=Chris|date=4 July 2023|accessdate=22 August 2023}}</ref>

Critics such as ''The A.V. Club''{{'}}s Kayleigh Dray praised the humorous style, with ''Rolling Stone''{{'}}s [[Alan Sepinwall]] describing the church scene as a highlight.<ref name="AVClub">{{cite web|url=https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-season-6-tv-review-netflix-charlie-brooker-1850540964|title=''Black Mirror'' season 6 review: Through the past, darkly|website=[[The A.V. Club]]|last=Dray|first=Kayleigh|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=20 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720184040/https://www.avclub.com/black-mirror-season-6-tv-review-netflix-charlie-brooker-1850540964|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="RS">{{cite web|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-mocks-netflix-annie-murphy-salma-hayek-1234770401/|title='Black Mirror' Season Six Takes Aim at Netflix But Feels Stuck in the Past|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|last=Sepinwall|first=Alan|author-link=Alan Sepinwall|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=30 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230630161000/https://www.rollingstone.com/tv-movies/tv-movie-reviews/black-mirror-season-6-review-mocks-netflix-annie-murphy-salma-hayek-1234770401/|url-status=live}}</ref> In ''Den of Geek'', Alec Bojalad summarised the episode as "cynical, caustic, and even charming", and Melanie McFarland—in ''Salon''—wrote that it was "hilarious, horrifying and left off-center enough from 2023's actuality to be off-putting".<ref name="DoG review">{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-joan-is-awful-review/|title=Black Mirror Season 6 Episode 1 Review: Joan Is Awful|work=[[Den of Geek]]|last=Bojalad|first=Alec|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=28 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230628123841/https://www.denofgeek.com/tv/black-mirror-joan-is-awful-review/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Salon">{{cite web|url=https://www.salon.com/2023/06/17/black-mirror-netflix-joan-is-awful-ai/|title=The best new 'Black Mirror' episode is a Netflix self-own that plays out our current AI nightmare|work=[[Salon.com|Salon]]|last=McFarland|first=Melanie|date=17 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=19 August 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230819022539/https://www.salon.com/2023/06/17/black-mirror-netflix-joan-is-awful-ai/|url-status=live}}</ref> Bootle found it to avoid tropes with its "winking sense of humour".<ref name="i"/> However, Power said the episode "isn't nearly as zingingly funny as it thinks it is".<ref name="Tele"/>

{{multiple image
| align       = right
| total_width = 250
| image1      = Annie Murphy (cropped).jpg
| alt1        = Annie Murphy
| image2      = Salma Hayek-9894.jpg
| alt2        = Salma Hayek Pinault
| footer      = The performances of [[Annie Murphy]] ''(left)'' and [[Salma Hayek Pinault]] ''(right)'' were widely praised by reviewers.}}
The acting was widely acclaimed, particularly that of Murphy and Hayek.<ref name="Tele"/><ref name="RS"/><ref name="BBC">{{cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Neil |title=Black Mirror season six review: Charlie Brooker's series is 'a show that revels in its twists' |url=https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20230614-black-mirror-season-six-review-charlie-brookers-series-is-a-show-that-revels-in-its-twists |website=[[BBC Culture]] |date=15 June 2023 |accessdate=23 August 2023 |archive-date=20 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720174319/https://www.bbc.com/culture/article/20230614-black-mirror-season-six-review-charlie-brookers-series-is-a-show-that-revels-in-its-twists |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="DoG review"/> Cranz said this was because they had different "comedic energy", so their characters were "brilliant [[foil (narrative)|foils]]".<ref name="Verge"/> Bootle praised Murphy's "perfect comic timing" and "outrage of a woman coming undone".<ref name="i"/> In a dissenting review for ''Vulture'', Ben Rosenstock found that Hayek "ultimately hurts the story" as her character "distracts from Joan" and is an "odd fit" for the programme. He criticised some of Hayek's jokes as "groaners".<ref name="Vulture">{{cite web|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-6-episode-1-joan-is-awful.html|title=''Black Mirror'' Season-Premiere Recap: Main-Character Syndrome|work=[[Vulture (magazine)|Vulture]]|last=Rosenstock|first=Ben|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=23 August 2023|archive-date=20 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720232347/https://www.vulture.com/article/black-mirror-recap-season-6-episode-1-joan-is-awful.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Reviewers were polarised on the episode's pacing and plot. Although Sepinwall approved of the "efficient use" of runtime, Bojalad felt it did not justify Joan's extreme behaviour in a church and Rosenstock said it should have been longer to reduce the exposition in the final 10 minutes.<ref name="RS"/><ref name="DoG review"/><ref name="Vulture"/> In a rarity for ''Black Mirror'', the ending is positive.<ref name="RS"/><ref name="DoG review"/> Rosenstock lauded it as a "fitting, mercifully happy" conclusion;<ref name="Vulture"/> Dray found the "wildly meta" ending to redeem the "meandering middle" parts.<ref name="AVClub"/> However, Cranz saw it as "a little [[wikt:twee|twee]]".<ref name="Verge"/>

At the [[4th Critics' Choice Super Awards]], "Joan Is Awful" won Best Science Fiction/Fantasy Series, Limited Series or Made-for-TV Movie and Annie Murphy won [[Critics' Choice Super Award for Best Actress in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Series|Best Actress in a Science Fiction/Fantasy Series, Limited Series or Made-for-TV Movie]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-04 |title=WINNERS ANNOUNCED FOR 4TH ANNUAL CRITICS CHOICE SUPER AWARDS HONORING SUPERHERO, SCIENCE FICTION/FANTASY, HORROR, AND ACTION MOVIES AND SERIES |url=https://www.criticschoice.com/2024/04/04/winners-announced-for-4th-annual-critics-choice-super-awards-honoring-superhero-science-fiction-fantasy-horror-and-action-movies-and-series/ |access-date=2024-04-04 |website=Critics Choice Association}}</ref>
